technical-summary: Two further live out-of-sequence-injection scenarios against fresh gpt-t1/gpt-t2 conversations both timed out (EXT-GPTAUTO-002) before the foreign-injection step was even reached in one case. E2 (gpt-t1): the trivial one-line baseline prompt itself never finished -- observation showed generating=true with stop-control visible for the full 3600s timeout, i.e. ChatGPT's own UI stayed in active-generation state indefinitely for a one-sentence reply. E3 (gpt-t2): the real turn timed out with completion-control visible but assistant-text-length=0 and an asymmetric observed-user-count=2 vs observed-assistant-count=3, suggesting the turn produced multiple internal assistant messages (plausibly a tool-call sub-message plus a final one) and the adapter's latest-assistant selection may have latched onto an intermediate/empty message rather than the true final reply -- a distinct, real edge case from the pure-stall cases, worth its own follow-up investigation separate from environmental throttling. In both cases the adapter behaved safely: chat-state settled to RECOVERING (not falsely completed, not silently stuck), tabs retained, no auto-resubmit, and the python process exited cleanly (0) with full diagnostics captured. Three consecutive real hour-long stalls across gpt-t1/gpt-t2 in one session (this @github review + these two) is a strong signal of either OpenAI-side throttling after heavy automated traffic or a project-level issue with these two test projects specifically -- not something further automated live retries will resolve; live testing against these two projects paused pending manual inspection.

technical-summary: Gateway state audit (via agent_task_list_requests and agent_task_session_list) found real, pre-existing violations of the never-leave-non-terminal-state requirement, unrelated to today's live testing. 5 gpt-auto requests dated 2026-08-06 through 2026-08-10 are still persisted as state=running despite cancel-requested=true and watchdog-state=not-started -- cancellation was requested days ago and never reconciled to a terminal state. Separately, 6 more gpt-auto sessions dated 2026-08-12 through 2026-08-14 are still persisted as state=active despite runtime-state=stale-non-live (their owning process is long gone). technical-summary: Fixed a live-confirmed bug (GP07): gpt-auto's submission-proof phase used a single fixed deadline from observation-loop start rather than being activity-aware, so a long prompt (~7000 chars) that was genuinely typed, submitted, and actively generating was falsely reported as ambiguous/timed-out because the fixed ~15s clock expired before DOM proof was polled. Added a new shared, reusable observation state machine (observation_engine.py) designed after a real external design-review critique: evidence carries independent capabilities -- PROGRESS (authoritative content change; resets the inactivity clock, reopens a terminal candidate, recovers a stall), SOFT_LIVENESS (inferred UI widget state; grants one bounded lease extension, never a repeated reset, never authoritative -- closes a real infinite-hang hole a naive design would have had if widget evidence could indirectly block failure by repeatedly renewing the same lease), TERMINAL_WITNESS (corroborating; can enter/verify a candidate, cannot reopen one). A monotonic progress_generation counter makes candidate verification race-resistant (edge-triggered, not level-triggered -- an unchanged fact re-observed every poll does not re-count as new evidence). Outcomes distinguish 'proved failed' from 'failed to prove what happened' (UNRESOLVED_STALL vs a hard failure), closing a duplicate-submission risk on retry. Wired into turn.py's _await_submission_proof with two new config fields (submission-proof-progress-lease-seconds default 5min, submission-proof-absolute-ceiling-seconds default 15min); _await_response deliberately not yet rewired through the same engine (lower-risk-first, sequenced separately).
